clips.text_zh: /biz/ 今晚個post問：未來10年只可以揸一樣，你揀Bitcoin定黃金？佢仲問點解你嗰樣好過另一樣。諗緊，我倉揸緊BTC又買咗少少XAU，黃金之前破頂，BTC就仲係sideways。10年period邊樣穩啲？黃金有幾千年歷史，BTC得十幾年，但數字稀缺。當rehersal題咁諗囉。
clips.text_en_b1: If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? The poster asks what makes your choice better than the other. Gold has thousands of years of history as a store of value. Bitcoin is only about 17 years old but has digital scarcity. Most anons are split between holding BTC and holding XAU long-term.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking BTC vs gold for the next decade

signal.rationale: 10-year hold framing implies long-term accumulation bias on BTC vs gold

clips.text_en_b2: If you were forced to hold just one asset for the next decade, would you back Bitcoin or gold, and what makes your choice objectively stronger? Gold carries thousands of years of monetary history, while Bitcoin is barely seventeen years old yet offers genuine digital scarcity. Most anons remain torn between long-term BTC and XAU, with some advocating a clean 50/50 split and others swearing by an all-in position.
clips.text_en_c1: A thread on /biz/ posed the following dilemma: if one were compelled to hold a single asset for the coming decade, should that asset be Bitcoin or gold, and on what grounds does it outperform the alternative? Gold, the traditionalists observe, carries several millennia of accumulated trust as a store of value, whereas Bitcoin, barely seventeen years old, derives its appeal from programmatic scarcity. The consensus among anons remains fractured: some advocate an equal split between BTC and XAU, whereas others insist that conviction demands an all-in position. Personally, I hold both, though given gold's recent breakout against BTC's sideways drift, the calculus warrants reconsideration.
clips.text_en_c2: Were one constrained to a single position for the coming decade, the rational choice between Bitcoin and gold hinges upon which property one values more: the venerable permanence of an ancient monetary store, or the algorithmic finality of digitally enforced scarcity. Gold, whose track record as a repository of value spans several millennia, benefits from entrenched institutional trust and demonstrably low correlation with sovereign monetary policy. Bitcoin, by contrast, possesses merely seventeen years of price discovery under its belt, yet its mathematically capped supply represents an unprecedented monetary experiment untethered from geopolitical vicissitudes. The poster, currently long BTC with a smaller allocation to XAU, frames this as an intellectual rehearsal.

clips.text_zh: /biz/ 有人話佢每星期都睇呢條片，問應該買咩。個片主講緊AI泡沫、歐洲崛起、英國玩完、USA衰落。如果佢講嘅嘢有20%啱，個portfolio應該短USA、長歐洲、長金、長BTC啦。但我仲係信Musk多過呢條友。NVDA照揸，TSLA等earnings再講。
clips.text_en_b1: Some anons have been posting this guy's content before. He covers the AI bubble and circular financing, the end of the USA and the rise of Europe, and the end of Britain. If you watch his videos every week, what do you actually invest in? He sounds like a boomer whose wife took everything and now he is doompilled about everything.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking what to buy when watching a doompilled macro YouTuber

signal.rationale: Doompilled macro takes imply long gold and short US equities as a hedge

clips.text_en_b2: Some anons have circulated this guy's content for months, covering the AI bubble and circular financing, the collapse of Britain, the rise of Europe, and the fall of the USA. If you watched his videos religiously, what would you actually buy? He comes across as a classic boomer whose wife cleaned him out and now radiates pure doompill energy. Most replies recommend going long gold and short US equities.
clips.text_en_c1: A persistent poster on /biz/ has been circulating a macroeconomic commentator whose weekly analyses address the AI bubble, Europe's ascendancy, Britain's terminal decline, and America's accelerating erosion. If even twenty percent of his thesis proves accurate, the logical portfolio adjustment would entail shorting US equities while going long Europe, gold, and BTC. Nevertheless, I place greater trust in Musk's ventures than in this particular pundit, whose outlook resembles that of a disillusioned boomer channelising personal grievance into prognostications. NVDA remains a core holding, TSLA awaits the next earnings cycle for resolution.
clips.text_en_c2: A recurring /biz/ commentator has resurfaced with his customary apocalyptic thesis, encompassing the AI bubble, the inexorable ascent of Europe, Britain's terminal decline, and the accelerating erosion of American hegemony. Were one to internalise even twenty percent of his prognostications, the prescribed portfolio would entail short US equities, long European indices, long gold, and long Bitcoin. Yet the presenter's dour fatalism, perpetually bearish and invariably vindicated by subsequent confirmation bias, suggests a man whose domestic circumstances have coloured his macroeconomic worldview. He reads less like an analyst than like a jilted spouse projecting personal grievance onto civilisational trends. The consensus on the board skews toward conventional hedges: NVDA remains a hold pending earnings volatility, gold accumulation continues apace, and TSLA awaits its quarterly catalyst.

clips.topic_zh: AI 殺 IQ 低嘅人
clips.text_zh: /g/ 有人話ChatGPT新AGI model會取代你。如果你冇160+ IQ，公司會發現呢樣嘢，南非式失業喺西方會到處都係。講到尾都係IQ問題。我A2-B1英文FE都未過，AI真係會搶我工程師嘅嘢？slope report都係我寫嘅，唔似得佢哋講到咁恐怖。
clips.text_en_b1: "AI is just a tool" works for 160+ IQ geniuses, but for the rest of us ChatGPT's new AGI model will replace us. Companies will start realizing this and South Africa style unemployment will become rampant across the West. Most anons agree that mid-tier office workers are the first to go. Engineers, trades, and physical labor stay safer for now.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread arguing AI replacement depends on your IQ

signal.rationale: AI labor commentary, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: The line "AI is merely a tool" only applies to 160+ IQ geniuses, while ChatGPT's new AGI model is set to replace everyone else. Once companies catch on, South Africa style unemployment will spread rapidly across the West, because this is fundamentally an IQ problem. Most anons reckon mid-tier office workers will vanish first, whereas engineers, trades, and physical labour should hold steady for now.
clips.text_en_c1: The prevailing argument on /g/ contends that ChatGPT's emerging AGI capabilities will render entire segments of the workforce obsolete, particularly those whose cognitive profiles fall below the 160 IQ threshold. Once corporate leadership internalises this reality, the inference goes, Western economies will witness unemployment patterns hitherto confined to South Africa. Most anons concur that mid-tier administrative occupations face displacement first, whereas engineers, skilled tradespeople, and those engaged in physical labour occupy considerably more defensible positions. As someone whose English remains stuck at A2-B1 and whose FE examinations loom uncomfortably, I find the doomer narrative somewhat overstated.
clips.text_en_c2: The proposition that ChatGPT's forthcoming model constitutes genuine artificial general intelligence has ignited considerable anxiety throughout the technology board. The argument runs thus: whilst sophisticated tools remain potent instruments for those possessing stratospheric cognitive capacity, individuals of merely average intellect will find their professional competencies progressively superseded by automated systems. The logical terminus of this trajectory, adherents contend, mirrors South Africa's chronic structural unemployment, where formal sector absorption has utterly failed to keep pace with demographic expansion. Most respondents concur that mid-tier administrative workers face the most acute displacement risk, whilst engineers, tradespeople, and those in physically demanding occupations enjoy comparatively greater insulation. The dissenting voice, a self-described professional engineer with adequate but unremarkable credentials, wonders whether such apocalyptic framing reflects technological reality or merely the customary online tendency toward catastrophism.

clips.text_zh: /biz/ 有人post條link話關稅收咗21兆美金？21兆喎，個數大到笑，GDP全球都冇咁多。呢啲post通常都係假數據呃like，但反映緊一件事：trade war繼續落去，USD會弱，金會繼續升。我DXY淡倉keep住，DXY弱就BTC強，simple。
clips.text_en_b1: A /biz/ anon posted that the US took in 21 trillion dollars from tariffs. The number is so absurd it broke containment on the board. Most replies point out global GDP is around 100 trillion, so 21 trillion from tariffs alone is nonsense. The real takeaway is traders are still pricing in tariff chaos and using gold and Bitcoin as the hedge against the dollar.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread questioning a viral '21 trillion from tariffs' tweet

signal.rationale: Macroeconomic noise post, not directly tradeable

clips.text_en_b2: A /biz/ anon claimed the US pulled in 21 trillion dollars from tariffs, a figure so absurd it broke containment across the board. Most replies noted that global GDP sits around 100 trillion, making 21 trillion from tariffs alone laughable nonsense. The genuine takeaway, however, is that traders are still hedging tariff chaos by loading up on gold and Bitcoin against a weakening dollar.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /biz/ circulated a claim that US tariffs had generated twenty-one trillion dollars in revenue, a figure so patently absurd that the thread rapidly escaped containment. Practically every respondent noted that global GDP totals roughly one hundred trillion, rendering the tariff figure not merely inflated but categorically implausible. Beneath the hyperbole, however, lies a genuine market signal: traders continue pricing in protracted trade-war turbulence and are accordingly gravitating toward gold and Bitcoin as hedges against dollar weakness. My DXY short remains intact; should the dollar falter further, BTC stands to benefit disproportionately.
clips.text_en_c2: A recent /biz/ submission claims that American tariff revenue has reached the rather preposterous figure of twenty-one trillion dollars, a sum so patently absurd that it immediately fractured the thread's coherence. For context, total global GDP hovers around one hundred trillion, rendering the alleged tariff haul not merely implausible but a statistical impossibility of the first order. Such fabrications, whilst transparently fictitious, serve as useful barometers of prevailing sentiment, since they reflect genuine anxiety about the trajectory of US trade policy. Traders have consequently positioned themselves defensively: the dollar index remains under sustained pressure, gold continues its measured ascent, and Bitcoin functions as an effective hedge against monetary debasement. The calculus is straightforward: diminished dollar strength, amplified BTC appeal, and the prudent allocator simply holds.

clips.text_zh: /pol/ 有人post咗個10年Trump journey list，由gamergate到epstein到china virus到winning。睇完我又諗返香港呢十年，2019到而家，唔好提啦。HK entertainment就係我嘅escape，AV女優同gossip先令我放鬂。Trump 4年做晒嘢？我淨係想要100k USD儲齊返Florida。
clips.text_en_b1: The OP recaps a 10 year journey: gamergate, sjw destroyed, infinity immigrants, crooked hillary, the golden escalator, pizzagate, winning the election, drain the swamp, charlottesville, china virus, kyle rittenhouse, everything woke goes to shit, lowest black unemployment. The poster says it was all for nothing. Anons are split between calling it cope and calling it the most based timeline ever.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread recapping 10 years of Trump-era culture war wins
clips.text_en_b2: The OP recaps a chaotic decade: gamergate, sjw wrecked, endless immigration, crooked hillary, the golden escalator, pizzagate, winning the election, drain the swamp, charlottesville, china virus, kyle rittenhouse, everything woke collapsing, and record low black unemployment. He concludes it was all for nothing, and anons are split between calling it cope and hailing it as the most based timeline ever.
clips.text_en_c1: A /pol/ retrospective enumerated the preceding decade through the lens of an online culture war: Gamergate, the perceived ascendancy of social justice activism, immigration controversies, political scandals, the escalator announcement, conspiracy theories, electoral victory, swamp-draining rhetoric, subsequent reckonings, pandemic response, and ultimately the symbolic metrics of lowest black unemployment. The original poster concludes that the cumulative effort amounted to little. Anons remain divided, some dismissing the sentiment as cope, others regarding it as the most substantive timeline in recent memory. If anything were salvaged, I would settle for a modest hundred thousand dollars and a quiet life in Florida.
clips.text_en_c2: An elaborate ten-year retrospective catalogues the cultural and political convulsions of the Trump era, an itinerary commencing with gamergate's origins, proceeding through perceived progressive overreach, the pivotal escalator announcement, pizzagate's viral proliferation, the unexpected electoral triumph, the perennially deferred swamp drainage, Charlottesville's enduring controversy, pandemic management, Kyle Rittenhouse's acquittal, and culminating in record-low black unemployment metrics. The original poster regards this entire sequence as ultimately futile, a decade of cultural warfare yielding negligible structural alteration. Respondents partition themselves between dismissing the sentiment as mere cope and celebrating what they term the most based timeline in living memory.

clips.text_zh: /fit/ 有條友post deadlift 220kg做咗兩下，PR係240kg。一個月冇deadlift，屋企練kettlebell clean同press。今日去gym特登試返，諗住做多吓。睇完好想即刻去gym，肥仔信話今晚一齊練，但我仲要温FE，beam design chapter未睇完。屌，30歲揀溫書定揸barbell。
clips.text_en_b1: The OP went deadlifting again and hit 220 kg for a double. His PR is 240 kg and he has gotten stronger since. He thinks he is better at single reps than higher reps. First time deadlifting in over a month because he has been training at home with kettlebell clean and press.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ progress post showing 220kg double deadlift PR attempt

signal.rationale: Lifting PR post, not a market trade

clips.text_en_b2: The OP finally hit the gym again and pulled 220 kg for a clean double, although his PR sits at 240 kg and he reckons he has grown stronger since. He performs better on singles than higher reps, and this marked his first deadlift session in over a month, since he has been training at home with kettlebell clean and press. Someone suggested he should have gone for 245 or 250.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ poster returned to the platform following an extended hiatus and immediately demonstrated that his strength had not merely persisted but actually compounded, deadlifting 220 kilograms for a clean double despite over a month away from the barbell. His established PR stands at 240, and he concedes that his physiology favours maximal efforts over higher-rep work, having maintained capacity through kettlebell cleans and overhead press at home. Critics correctly observe that the rational next step would have been an attempt at 245 or 250 to probe his true ceiling, yet with FE examinations looming and beam design chapters remaining unread, such aspirations remain indefinitely deferred.
clips.text_en_c2: The original poster returned to conventional barbell training after an extended hiatus from deadlifting, having subsisted for over a month upon home-based kettlebell clean and press work, and successfully completed two repetitions at two hundred and twenty kilograms, approaching his established personal record of two hundred and forty. His self-assessment suggests greater proficiency in maximal single-rep efforts than in higher-volume sets, an observation consistent with neural adaptations favouring peak force production over work capacity. Observers reasonably suggest he ought to have tested his absolute ceiling at two hundred forty-five or two hundred fifty kilograms rather than settling for a conservative double.

clips.text_zh: /a/ 有人post Gochiusa，話Koi努力做緊season 4、movie、同埋下一個McDonald's crossover。Gochiusa我未睇過，但呢種輕鬆日常番好啱我夜晚relax。FE溫到攰就開嚟睇，lol。肥仔信話佢睇Demon Slayer，我就鍾意呢類CGDCT。
clips.text_en_b1: It's another beautiful day knowing Koi is working hard on season 4, the movie, and the next McDonald's collab for Gochiusa. Anons are hyped because the series has been on a slow production cycle for years. Some are worried the studio might change staff again. Others just want a clean bluray release with good subs before the next season drops.
clips.source_hint: /a/ hype thread about Gochiusa season 4, movie, and McDonald's collab
clips.text_en_b2: It is genuinely reassuring knowing Koi is grinding away on season 4, the upcoming movie, and another McDonald's collab for Gochiusa. Anons are thrilled, although the franchise has been stuck on a painfully slow production cycle for years, and some worry the studio might shuffle staff yet again. Others simply want a clean bluray release with solid subs before the next season lands.
clips.text_en_c1: Members of /a/ celebrated the confirmation that Koi's production apparatus remains engaged with season 4, the accompanying film, and a forthcoming McDonald's collaboration for the Gochiusa franchise. Given the notoriously protracted production cycle that has characterised recent seasons, anticipation among the community is palpably elevated, notwithstanding lingering anxieties regarding potential staff turnover at the studio. A faction of viewers prioritises a clean Blu-ray release accompanied by competent subs ahead of the next broadcast, whereas others simply yearn for the gentle, restorative qualities that this particular CGDCT offering reliably delivers after a gruelling FE study session.
clips.text_en_c2: The announcement that Koi Studio continues its diligent production of Gochiusa season four, alongside the feature film and a forthcoming McDonald's promotional collaboration, has occasioned considerable enthusiasm on the anime board, particularly given the franchise's notoriously protracted development cycle. Long-suffering devotees, accustomed to the studio's deliberate artistic pacing, remain nevertheless anxious about potential personnel turnover within the production committee, since staff transitions have historically affected tonal consistency in similar adaptations. The most pragmatic among them advocate simply for a meticulously authored Blu-ray release featuring exemplary subtitle work before the subsequent season premieres. For newcomers encountering the property, its gentle quotidian rhythms offer precisely the cerebral rest that intensive examination revision demands, rendering it an ideal counterpoint to Demon Slayer's bombastic intensity. The series exemplifies CGDCT at its most refined.
